1	# Use Case: View Veterinarians
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	**Use Case ID:** UC-002   
6	**Use Case Name:** View Veterinarians   
7	**Primary Actor:** Visitor   
8	**Goal:** Browse the list of veterinarians employed at the clinic along with their specialties.   
9	**Status:** Approved   
10	**Requirements:** [FR-003, NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-003, C-010, C-011](../requirements.md)
11	
12	## Preconditions
13	
14	- At least one veterinarian is recorded in the system (see A1 otherwise).
15	
16	## Main Success Scenario
17	
18	1. Visitor clicks the "Veterinarians" link in the navigation bar.
19	2. System retrieves the first set of veterinarians.
20	3. System renders the veterinarians grid showing, for each vet, the first name, last name, and a comma-separated list of
21	   specialties (or "none" if no specialties are held).
22	4. As the Visitor scrolls toward the end of the grid, the system fetches and appends the next chunk of veterinarians
23	   until all entries have been loaded.
24	
25	## Alternative Flows
26	
27	### A1: No Veterinarians Registered
28	
29	**Trigger:** The clinic has no veterinarians recorded (step 2).
30	**Flow:**
31	
32	1. System renders the veterinarians grid with no rows.
33	2. Use case ends.
34	
35	## Postconditions
36	
37	### Success Postconditions
38	
39	- The veterinarians grid is rendered with all loaded entries.
40	- No data is modified.
41	
42	### Failure Postconditions
43	
44	- On data-access errors, the application error view is shown and no vet list is displayed.
45	
46	## Business Rules
47	
48	### BR-001: Lazy Loading
49	
50	Realizes [GR-002: Lazy Loading of Lists](../business_rules.md#gr-002-lazy-loading-of-lists).
51	
52	The list in question is the veterinarians grid.
53	
54	### BR-002: Specialty Ordering
55	
56	Realizes [GR-003: Deterministic Ordering](../business_rules.md#gr-003-deterministic-ordering).
57	
58	The order in question is a vet's specialties, alphabetically by name.
59	
60	### BR-003: Anonymous Access
61	
62	Realizes [GR-001: Anonymous Access](../business_rules.md#gr-001-anonymous-access).
63

1	# Development View
2	
3	**Question:** How is the code organized, built, and kept honest?  
4	**Artifacts:** this document, [`testing.md`](testing.md) (the testing half of this
5	view), `CLAUDE.md` (the short form an agent always has loaded)  
6	**Notation:** Markdown  
7	**For the agent:** the most important view, and the one to read **before writing
8	anything** in `src/main/java/`. Every rule here saves a correction in every use
9	case.
10	
11	Most of what follows is **enforced executably** by
12	`src/test/java/ai/unifiedprocess/petclinic/ArchitectureTest.java` (ArchUnit, runs
13	with `./mvnw test`). Each rule names the section it comes from, so a failure
14	points straight back here. If you change a convention below, change the matching
15	rule in the same commit — a rule that contradicts this document is the rule
16	that's wrong.
17	
18	These rules are the harness for use cases that have **not been written yet**, so
19	a rule may legitimately match no classes — on a branch where only UC-001 exists
20	there is no `domain` package to check. `src/test/resources/archunit.properties`
21	sets `archRule.failOnEmptyShould=false` for exactly that reason: a rule about
22	code that does not exist yet is vacuously satisfied, the same stance the
23	traceability sensors take towards a use case that is not `Done` yet.
24	
25	## Technology stack
26	
27	| Concern               | Choice                                               | Version      | Decided in                                                |
28	|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
29	| Language / runtime    | Java                                                 | 25           | C-001                                                     |
30	| Application framework | Spring Boot                                          | 4.1.1        | C-002                                                     |
31	| UI                    | Vaadin Flow (server-side Java views)                 | 25.2         | [ADR-002](adr/ADR-002-vaadin-flow-server-side-ui.md)      |
32	| Database access       | jOOQ, generated from the schema                      | 3.21         | [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-jooq-instead-of-jpa.md)             |
33	| Schema migration      | Flyway                                               | Boot-managed | [ADR-003](adr/ADR-003-flyway-owns-the-schema.md)          |
34	| Database              | PostgreSQL (`postgres:17-alpine` for build and test) | 17           | C-005                                                     |
35	| Build                 | Maven (wrapper), single module                       | —            | —                                                         |
36	| View tests            | Vaadin Browserless Testing                           | Vaadin BOM   | [ADR-006](adr/ADR-006-two-test-layers-merged-coverage.md) |
37	| Browser tests         | Playwright + Drama Finder                            | 1.1          | [ADR-006](adr/ADR-006-two-test-layers-merged-coverage.md) |
38	| Architecture tests    | ArchUnit                                             | 1.5          | —                                                         |
39	| Coverage              | JaCoCo, merged across both test layers               | 0.8          | —                                                         |
40	| Quality gate          | SonarQube Cloud                                      | —            | —                                                         |
41	
42	Exact versions are in `pom.xml`, which wins over this table.
43	
44	## Module layout
45	
46	Single Maven module, **package by feature** under
47	`ai.unifiedprocess.petclinic`. The features follow the use cases — `owner`,
48	`pet`, `visit`, `vet`, `welcome` — and each is one package with exactly two
49	sub-packages:
50	
51	- **`ui`** — Vaadin views, forms, and other UI components. One view per use
52

trajectory.message:
I wrote the UC-002 code and tests, but none of it has been compiled or run. This environment has no Docker, so jOOQ code generation can't run. The sensor build also fails offline because a Maven plugin isn't cached. The `Status:` line is untouched.

**What I added**
- `vet/domain/Vet.java`: a `Serializable` record holding id, first name, last name and the list of specialty names.
- `vet/domain/VetRepository.java`: a read-only `@Repository` with `findPage(offset, limit)` and `count()`.
  - It loads each vet's specialties in the same query with `multiset(...).convertFrom(...)`, so there's no N+1.
  - Specialties are ordered by name (BR-002), and vets by last name, first name, then id, so scrolling is stable.
- `vet/ui/VetsView.java`: the `/vets` route inside `MainLayout`, with a grid of First Name, Last Name and Specialties. The specialties cell is comma-separated, or "none" when empty.
  - The grid loads lazily through a callback data provider (BR-001).
  - There is no login, so access is anonymous (BR-003).
  - A vet-less database gives an empty grid (A1).
- `UC002ViewVeterinariansTest`: a browserless test against the seed data. It checks six rows are shown, the "none" and "dentistry, surgery" cells, and that the table is alphabetical.

The "Veterinarians" nav item already pointed at `vets`, so I didn't touch `MainLayout`.

**What still needs doing**
1. Run `./mvnw verify` somewhere with Docker. The repository imports `database.Tables.*`, which I couldn't check against generated sources.
2. Run the `aiup-vaadin-jooq:coverage-check` skill, then set the `Status:` line. The hooks require the audit first.
3. A Playwright `*IT` for UC-002 is not written; no test case covers it yet.
